note: Roll-up index. Full per-concept registers live in the four subdirectories; this file only summarizes and records cross-concept (shared-layer) impacts. Candidate IDs everywhere are provisional; canon is never minted in concept work. concepts.title: fable · Atlas
concepts.design_contract_summary: Settings as a reference manual: numbered sections, marginalia column, managers as appendices. Native families: Context & Instructions, Memory, Personas, Goal & Automation, Crew, Permissions & FileSafe, Back Seat Driver, plus the core group.

concepts.title: fable · Mission Control
concepts.design_contract_summary: Settings as an operational console: health strip, triage stack, command palette, minimap. Native families: Notifications & Sounds, Sound Library/uploads/packs, Appearance with custom TOML themes, Spellcheck & Dictionaries, Desktop/Tray/Window, Teacher/Help, plus Media beyond assignment and the core group.

concepts.title: fable · Focus Stack
concepts.design_contract_summary: Settings as layered attention: one live surface, visible layer spine, disclosure is navigation. Native families: File Manager/Editor, Terminal, LSP, Formatters, Commands & Shortcuts, MCP, Skills, Plugins, Tools, Testing & Debug, plus the core group.

concepts.title: fable · Ledger
concepts.design_contract_summary: Settings as an object browser: records plus a persistent right inspector, zero motion. Native families: Storage & Retention, Backup & Restore, Settings Lifecycle, History & Sessions, Runtime Artifacts, Source Control/Worktrees, GitHub Actions, Containers & Registries, Web/Search/Fetch, Search Index, Workspace Cleanup, Future Server Module Shell, plus the core group.

cross_concept_findings.finding: Shared provider semantics module prevents behavioral drift
cross_concept_findings.detail: All four concepts resolve installation, update-lifecycle, free-route, auth-boundary, and requested/effective semantics through _shared/pm-provider.js, which exports no HTML or CSS. The ten update states, six free-route states, and the seven-condition verify checklist exist in exactly one place. Candidate DRY families InstallationCard/CapabilityEvidence/RequestedEffectiveInspector should be specified as semantics + per-surface composition, not shared markup.

cross_concept_findings.finding: Deterministic deep-link contract is a production candidate
cross_concept_findings.detail: The hash route grammar (#/dest|manager|setting|search + scenario/fixture/trigger/focus/instant/pin params) gave every required state a stable, automatable address and real Back/forward history. A production equivalent belongs in the navigation family of the command catalog (cmd.settings.navigate payload shape), and the test matrix should key on it.

cross_concept_findings.finding: Title-bar notification stack lives in the shared shell
cross_concept_findings.detail: Destination test-sends land in the shared title-bar stack + sprout inbox (F3-460/461 canon), proving notification wiring without any concept growing a second notification surface. No corner stacks, status-bar bells, or notification panels exist anywhere in the folder.

cross_concept_findings.finding: Scenario x fixture-overlay x route are orthogonal axes
cross_concept_findings.detail: Eight whole-dataset scenarios, twelve additive fixture overlays (re-applied after every scenario rebuild), and the route contract compose deterministically. This kept the probe matrix O(states) instead of O(states x surfaces) and is a candidate pattern for the production test fixtures.

Inventory counts disagree across artifacts (817 in the PM7 build assertion, 818/819 in sidecar/embedded payloads, 824 in the PlanUnit text, 826 in Plans/settings_inventory.json). The packet-required rows added here (sounds, desktop, BSD, storage, backup, lifecycle, formatters, web limits, MCP transport) exist in no canon count. Flagged in each per-concept register.

cross_concept_findings.finding: Shared trigger registry needs owner-scoped refs in production
cross_concept_findings.detail: Demo triggers use loosely-scoped refs (provider id, installation path, destination id). The MCP-vs-provider reconnect ambiguity found during the build was resolved by id-precedence in the shared layer; production commands must carry typed, owner-scoped payloads instead.
